introduction: On this Sunday, Isaiah announces that God's house will be a house of prayer for all peoples. In the Gospel, a Canaanite woman, a foreigner, begs Jesus to heal her daughter; she persists with humility and faith, and Jesus says, Woman, great is your faith. Paul tells us that the gifts and the call of God are irrevocable. Let us pray with the persistence and faith of this mother.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God's house is a house of prayer for all peoples. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be a house of prayer and welcome for people of every nation. Let us pray to the Lord.
For parents who pray for their sick or troubled children: that they may never give up, like the Canaanite mother. Let us pray to the Lord.
For foreigners, migrants and all who feel like outsiders: that they may find welcome in the Church. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the Jewish people, whose call from God is irrevocable: that God may bless them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that our faith may be persistent, humble and great. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you welcome all peoples into your house of prayer. Give us the persistent faith of the Canaanite woman, and open our hearts to every person. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Great is your faith
reflection.body:
Isaiah speaks of foreigners who join themselves to the Lord, and God promises: "I will bring these to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer." And he gives a reason that Jesus later quotes in the temple: "for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples." From the beginning, God's plan included everyone.

In the Gospel, Jesus travels into the region of Tyre and Sidon, outside Israel. A Canaanite woman, a foreigner, comes crying out: "Have mercy on me, Lord, you son of David! My daughter is severely possessed by a demon!" At first Jesus does not answer. The disciples want him to send her away. Jesus says that his mission is first to Israel.

But the woman does not give up. She kneels before him: "Lord, help me." Jesus answers with a hard saying, using a common expression of the time that set Israel apart from other nations. The woman is not offended. She turns his words into a humble argument: "Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from their masters' table." She asks only for crumbs, and she believes that even crumbs from Jesus are enough.

Jesus is moved: "Woman, great is your faith! Be it done to you even as you desire." And her daughter is healed. An outsider, a mother praying for her child, becomes a model of faith for everyone.

Paul, writing to Gentile Christians, reminds them that God has not abandoned the Jewish people: "For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable." God's purpose, he says, is to "have mercy on all."

This week, bring to God someone you have been praying for, and do not give up. Pray with humility and persistence, like this mother. And notice who is treated as an outsider around you, and make them welcome.
